items.name: theme
items.title: Theme
items.description: p0seid0n design tokens: the nine --p0seid0n-* colours, control and panel radii, popup shadow, and the Tailwind v4 @theme inline bridge.
items.docs: Import the stylesheet once, in the same file that imports Tailwind. Light and dark follow color-scheme: the OS preference by default, or a .light or .dark class on the html element. There are no dark: variants, so overriding any --p0seid0n-* value re-themes every component, including at runtime.

items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.description: Ink-filled primary, control-grey secondary, transparent ghost and danger button in three sizes, with loading and leading/trailing slots.
items.docs: Use variant primary, secondary, ghost or danger and size sm, md or lg. Loading sets aria-busy, disables interaction and leaves the progress slot usable. Use the leading and trailing slots for icons; the component ships none. A click handler passed from the parent is not called while loading or disabled.

files.content:
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, useAttrs } from 'vue'
import type { Component } from 'vue'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { buttonVariants } from './variants'
import type { ButtonSize, ButtonVariant } from './variants'

defineOptions({ inheritAttrs: false })

export type ButtonProps = {
  variant?: ButtonVariant
  size?: ButtonSize
  /** Rendered element or component. Links pass as: 'a'. */
  as?: string | Component
  /** Native button type; ignored when `as` is not a button. */
  type?: 'button' | 'submit' | 'reset'
  /** Disables interaction and marks the button as busy. */
  loading?: boolean
  disabled?: boolean
}

const props = withDefaults(defineProps<ButtonProps>(), {
  variant: 'primary',
  size: 'md',
  as: 'button',
  type: 'button',
  loading: false,
  disabled: false,
})

const attrs = useAttrs()

// The click listener is attached by this component so that `loading` and
// `disabled` also block it for non-button roots such as links.
const forwarded = computed(() => {
  const rest = { ...attrs }
  delete rest.class
  delete rest.onClick
  return rest
})

const isNativeButton = computed(() => props.as === 'button')
const isInert = computed(() => props.disabled || props.loading)

function onClick(event: MouseEvent): void {
  if (isInert.value) {
    event.preventDefault()
    return
  }
  ;(attrs.onClick as ((event: MouseEvent) => void) | undefined)?.(event)
}
</script>

<template>
  <component
    :is="as"
    v-bind="forwarded"
    :type="isNativeButton ? type : undefined"
    :class="cn(buttonVariants({ variant, size }), $attrs.class as string | undefined)"
    :disabled="isNativeButton ? isInert : undefined"
    :aria-disabled="isInert ? 'true' : undefined"
    :aria-busy="loading ? 'true' : undefined"
    @click="onClick"
  >
    <slot name="progress" />
    <slot name="leading" />
    <slot />
    <slot name="trailing" />
  </component>
</template>

export { default as Button } from './Button.vue'
export { buttonVariants } from './variants'
export type { ButtonSize, ButtonVariant } from './variants'
export type { ButtonProps } from './Button.vue'

<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, useAttrs } from 'vue'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'

defineOptions({ inheritAttrs: false })

const attrs = useAttrs()
const forwarded = computed(() => {
  const rest = { ...attrs }
  delete rest.class
  return rest
})

export type InputProps = {
  /** Marks the field as invalid and paints the border with the danger colour. */
  invalid?: boolean
  disabled?: boolean
  id?: string
}

withDefaults(defineProps<InputProps>(), {
  invalid: false,
  disabled: false,
  id: undefined,
})

const model = defineModel<string | number>({ default: '' })
const emit = defineEmits<{ input: [event: Event] }>()

function onInput(event: Event): void {
  model.value = (event.target as HTMLInputElement).value
  emit('input', event)
}
</script>

<template>
  <input
    v-bind="forwarded"
    :id="id"
    v-model="model"
    :disabled="disabled"
    :aria-invalid="invalid ? 'true' : undefined"
    :class="
      cn(
        'h-11 w-full rounded-control border border-line bg-control px-3 text-[15px] text-ink',
        'placeholder:text-ink-muted',
        'outline-none focus-visible:border-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-solid focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-ink',
        'aria-[invalid=true]:border-danger aria-[invalid=true]:focus-visible:outline-danger',
        'disabled:cursor-default disabled:opacity-55',
        'transition-[background-color,color,border-color,box-shadow] duration-150 motion-reduce:transition-none',
        $attrs.class as string | undefined,
      )
    "
    @input="onInput"
  />
</template>

import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuPortal } from 'reka-ui'
import { popupSurface } from './styles'

defineOptions({ inheritAttrs: false })

export type DropdownMenuContentProps = {
  align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end'
  /** Gap between the trigger and the popup, in pixels. */
  sideOffset?: number
  side?: 'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left'
  /** Overrides the 160px minimum width from the reference menu. */

const props = withDefaults(defineProps<DropdownMenuContentProps>(), {

  sideOffset: 8,
  side: 'bottom',

}

      :side="props.side"

<script setup lang="ts">
import { DialogRoot } from 'reka-ui'
import { provideDialogBehaviour } from './behaviour'

defineOptions({ inheritAttrs: false })

export type DialogProps = {
  /** Closes when the pointer goes down outside the panel. */
  closeOnOutside?: boolean
  closeOnEsc?: boolean
}

const props = withDefaults(defineProps<DialogProps>(), {
  closeOnOutside: true,
  closeOnEsc: true,
})

// Passed as thunks rather than as props so the flags are read at event time.
provideDialogBehaviour({
  closeOnOutside: () => props.closeOnOutside,
  closeOnEsc: () => props.closeOnEsc,
})

const model = defineModel<boolean>({ default: false })
</script>

items.description: Trigger strip and panels with arrow key navigation.
items.docs: Bind with v-model and give each TabsTrigger and TabsContent a matching value. items.name: toast
items.title: Toast
items.description: Self-contained notification stack with a provider, useToast composable and three variants.
items.docs: Wrap the app in ToastProvider, then call useToast().toast({ title, description, variant, action, duration }). The provider keeps at most max notifications (3 by default) and drops the oldest first; duration defaults to 4000ms and zero keeps one open. variant danger uses the theme danger colour. The stack sits at z-60 so it stays above dialogs.

<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, provide } from 'vue'
import { toastKey, type ToastApi, type ToastOptions } from './context'
import { createToastStack, provideToastStack } from './stack'
import Toaster from './Toaster.vue'

export type ToastProviderProps = {
  /** Milliseconds a notification stays open, overridable per call. */
  duration?: number
  /** Oldest notifications beyond this count are dropped immediately. */
  max?: number
}

const props = withDefaults(defineProps<ToastProviderProps>(), {
  duration: 4000,
  max: 3,
})

const stack = createToastStack()
provideToastStack(stack)

function toast(options: ToastOptions): string {
  return stack.push(options, props.duration, props.max)
}

const api = computed<ToastApi>(() => ({
  toast,
  dismiss: stack.dismiss,
  dismissAll: stack.dismissAll,
}))
provide(toastKey, api.value)

defineExpose({ toast, dismiss: stack.dismiss, dismissAll: stack.dismissAll })
</script>

<template>
  <slot />
  <Toaster />
</template>

import type { ToastVariant } from './context'

export const toastViewport = [

].join(' ')

  'motion-safe:animate-[p0seid0n-toast-in_150ms_ease-out]',
].join(' ')

const variantAccent: Record<ToastVariant, string> = {
  default: 'bg-line',

  danger: 'bg-danger',
}

/** Left edge marker that tints the card without recolouring the text. */
export function toastAccent(variant: ToastVariant): string {

}

items.name: sparkline
items.title: Sparkline
items.description: Hand-written SVG bar strip for a numeric series, with median-based scaling and an optional baseline.
items.docs: Pass values as a number array; the component never formats or formats labels for you. Bars fill 60% of each slot and the series is pinned to the right edge when slots is larger than the data. The value axis is capped at median x 3 so a few spikes cannot flatten the rest; with one or two samples it falls back to the maximum. An empty array renders no path but keeps its size, a single sample renders one full-width-relative bar. Set ariaLabel to expose role img; without it the graphic is aria-hidden.

files.content:
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed } from 'vue'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { sparklinePath } from './geometry'

defineOptions({ inheritAttrs: false })

export type SparklineTone = 'default' | 'accent' | 'accent-alt'

export type SparklineProps = {
  values: readonly number[]
  /** Upper bound of the value axis; defaults to the median-based scale. */
  max?: number
  /** Draws a 1px rule at the bottom of the strip. */
  baseline?: boolean
  tone?: SparklineTone
  /** Accessible name. Without it the graphic is hidden from assistive technology. */
  ariaLabel?: string
  /** Bars are laid out across this many slots; the newest sits at the right edge. */
  slots?: number
  /**
   * Strip height, `font-size` relative. The reference puts the strip beside the 26px
   * value text, so `0.7em` there is about 18px; inside a Stat the figure slot
   * inherits that font size, and standalone use should set a font size on the parent.
   */
  height?: string
}

const props = withDefaults(defineProps<SparklineProps>(), {
  max: undefined,
  baseline: false,
  tone: 'default',
  ariaLabel: undefined,
  slots: undefined,
  height: '0.7em',
})

const toneClass = computed(
  () =>
    ({
      default: 'text-ink-faint',
      accent: 'text-accent',
      'accent-alt': 'text-danger',
    })[props.tone],
)

const path = computed(() =>
  sparklinePath({ values: props.values, slots: props.slots, max: props.max }),
)
const viewWidth = computed(() =>
  Math.max(props.slots ?? props.values.length, props.values.length, 1),
)

const labelled = computed(() => props.ariaLabel !== undefined)
</script>

<template>
  <svg
    v-bind="$attrs"
    :viewBox="`0 0 ${viewWidth} 1`"
    :style="{ height: props.height }"
    preserveAspectRatio="none"
    :class="
      cn(
        'block w-full',
        props.baseline ? 'border-b border-line' : undefined,
        toneClass,
        $attrs.class as string | undefined,
      )
    "
    :role="labelled ? 'img' : undefined"
    :aria-label="props.ariaLabel"
    :aria-hidden="labelled ? undefined : 'true'"
  >
    <path :d="path" fill="currentColor" />
  </svg>
</template>

export { default as Sparkline } from './Sparkline.vue'
export { median, scaleTop, sparklinePath } from './geometry'
export type { SparklineOptions } from './geometry'
export type { SparklineProps, SparklineTone } from './Sparkline.vue'

items.name: theme-provider
items.title: Theme Provider
items.description: Three-state theme state (system, light, dark) with a matching inline script for the first paint.
items.docs: Wrap the app in ThemeProvider and read state with useTheme(): theme is the stored choice, resolvedTheme is what is painted. setTheme writes localStorage only when the choice changes, and system removes the key so the OS preference keeps driving the page. Inline the themeScript() string in head before your bundle to avoid a flash on reload; it only touches the html element, so hydration has nothing to disagree with.

files.content:
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, onBeforeUnmount, onMounted, provide, ref, watch } from 'vue'
import {
  DEFAULT_STORAGE_KEY,
  applyThemeToDocument,
  readStoredTheme,
  systemTheme,
  type ResolvedTheme,
  type ThemeChoice,
} from './theme'
import { themeKey, type ThemeApi } from './context'

export type ThemeProviderProps = {
  storageKey?: string
  /** Used when nothing is stored yet. */
  defaultTheme?: ThemeChoice
  /** Attribute mirrored onto `html` so CSS can target the explicit choice. */
  attribute?: string
}

const props = withDefaults(defineProps<ThemeProviderProps>(), {
  storageKey: DEFAULT_STORAGE_KEY,
  defaultTheme: 'system',
  attribute: 'data-theme',
})

const theme = ref<ThemeChoice>(props.defaultTheme)
const resolvedTheme = ref<ResolvedTheme>('light')

let media: MediaQueryList | undefined
let hydrated = false

function sync(): void {
  resolvedTheme.value = applyThemeToDocument(theme.value, props.attribute)
}

function setTheme(next: ThemeChoice): void {
  theme.value = next
}

// localStorage is written only when the choice changes, not on every system
// preference event: those are not user decisions and must not pin `system`.
watch(theme, (next) => {
  sync()
  if (!hydrated) return
  try {
    if (next === 'system') localStorage.removeItem(props.storageKey)
    else localStorage.setItem(props.storageKey, next)
  } catch {
    // A blocked storage backend still needs the in-memory choice to apply.
  }
})

function onSystemChange(): void {
  // Only matters while following the system; a pinned choice ignores it.
  if (theme.value === 'system') sync()
}

onMounted(() => {
  theme.value = readStoredTheme(props.storageKey)
  sync()
  hydrated = true
  media = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')
  media.addEventListener('change', onSystemChange)
})

onBeforeUnmount(() => {
  media?.removeEventListener('change', onSystemChange)
})

const api: ThemeApi = {
  theme,
  resolvedTheme,
  setTheme,
  systemTheme,
  storageKey: props.storageKey,
}
provide(themeKey, api)

const ready = computed(() => hydrated)
defineExpose({ ready, theme, resolvedTheme, setTheme })
</script>

<template>
  <slot />
</template>

export { default as ThemeProvider } from './ThemeProvider.vue'
export { useTheme, DEFAULT_STORAGE_KEY } from './context'
export { applyThemeToDocument, readStoredTheme, systemTheme, themeScript } from './theme'
export type { ThemeApi } from './context'
export type { ThemeProviderProps } from './ThemeProvider.vue'
export type { ResolvedTheme, ThemeChoice } from './theme'
